# Folate deficiency

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Hematology and oncology > Red blood cell disorders > Folate deficiency*

[Original Article Link](/library/qL0CAg)

---

## Summary

<u>Folate</u> deficiency is most commonly caused by <u>malnutrition</u>, e.g., in individuals with insufficient dietary intake or <u>alcohol use disorder</u>. Patients typically present with <u>signs of anemia</u> (e.g., fatigue). Initial <u>laboratory studies</u> show <u>macrocytic anemia</u>, circulating <u>megaloblasts</u>, and, in some cases, <u>pancytopenia</u>. Low <u>fasting</u> serum <u>folate</u> levels confirm the diagnosis, but <u>sensitivity</u> is limited; if levels are normal, <u>RBC</u> <u>folate</u> or plasma <u>homocysteine</u> testing should be performed. <u>Treatment of folate deficiency</u> consists of oral <u>folate</u> replacement and increasing dietary intake of <u>folate-rich foods</u> (e.g., leafy green vegetables, fruits, and fortified foods).

---

## Physiology

* <u>Folate</u>: <u>coenzyme</u> in single-carbon transfers and <u>methylation</u> reactions → <u>DNA synthesis</u> and <u>amino acid metabolism</u> [[1]](/library/GTYBHo)

* Active form: <u>tetrahydrofolate</u> (<u>THF</u>), obtained after reduction of <u>folate</u> by <u>dihydrofolate reductase</u>

* Sources: <u>folate-rich foods</u>

* Absorption: in the <u>jejunum</u>

* Storage: <u>liver</u> (stores <u>folate</u> for up to three months, after which time signs and symptoms of deficiency begin to appear)

---

## Etiology

* <u>Malnutrition</u>

* Insufficient intake (e.g., “tea and toast” diet)

* <u>Alcohol use disorder</u>

* <u>Malabsorption</u>

* <u>Small bowel</u> disease (e.g., <u>tropical sprue</u>, <u>celiac disease</u>, <u>inflammatory bowel disease</u>)

* Surgical procedures (e.g., resection of the <u>small intestine</u>, <u>gastric bypass</u>)

* Increased requirement

* <u>Pregnancy</u> or lactation

* Severe <u>hemolytic anemia</u>

* Exfoliative <u>skin</u> disease (e.g., <u>eczema</u>) [[2]](/library/vTYAso)[[3]](/library/6kdjKJ0)

* Medication-related [[4]](/library/JmasgO)

* <u>Methotrexate</u>

* <u>Antiepileptic drugs</u> (e.g., <u>phenytoin</u>)

* <u>Sulfonamides</u>

* <u>Trimethoprim</u>

---

## Pathophysiology

Decreased <u>folate</u> levels lead to decreased levels of <u>tetrahydrofolate</u>. This, in turn, leads to the following effects:




* ↓ <u>DNA</u> synthesis → megaloblastic <u>erythropoiesis</u> → <u>megaloblastic anemia</u> (and ↓ in other cell lines)

* ↓ <u>Methionine</u> and ↑ <u>homocysteine</u> → <u>endothelial</u> damage → ↑ risk of cardiovascular disease and <u>thromboembolic events</u>

* During <u>fetal development</u>: <u>nucleotide</u> synthesis impairment → <u>neural tube defects</u>

* Aberrant <u>DNA methylation</u> → ↑ risk of cancer  [[5]](/library/FTYgso)[[6]](/library/8TYOso)

Methionine cycle

---

## Clinical features

* <u>Signs of anemia</u> (e.g., fatigue, <u>pallor</u>)

* <u>Glossitis</u>

* Maternal deficiency: fetal <u>spina bifida</u> or <u>anencephaly</u>





> [!NOTE]
> Unlike <u>vitamin B<sub>12</sub> deficiency</u>, <u>folate</u> deficiency does not typically cause neurological symptoms; rarely, neuropsychiatric conditions (e.g., cognitive impairment, <u>depression</u>) or <u>peripheral neuropathy</u> can occur. [[7]](/library/8kdOpJ0)[[8]](/library/ukdppJ0)

---

## Diagnosis

### Initial studies [[3]](/library/6kdjKJ0)




* Evaluate <u>CBC</u> and morphology.

* <u>CBC</u>: <u>macrocytic anemia</u> (<u>MCV</u> > 100 Î¼mÂ³)

* <u>Peripheral blood smear</u>: oval <u>macrocytes</u>, circulating <u>megaloblasts</u>; , and <u>hypersegmented neutrophils</u>

* Rule out <u>vitamin B<sub>12</sub> deficiency</u>.

* <u>Vitamin B<sub>12</sub></u> level

* <u>Methylmalonic acid</u> (MMA): normal in <u>folate</u> deficiency  [[9]](/library/widhFp0)





> [!NOTE]
> In <u>folate</u> deficiency, MMA is normal; in <u>vitamin B<sub>12</sub> deficiency</u>, MMA is elevated.




### Diagnostic confirmation [[2]](/library/vTYAso)[[3]](/library/6kdjKJ0)




* <u>Fasting</u> serum <u>folate</u> level (first line): < 3 ng/mL (limited <u>sensitivity</u>)  [[2]](/library/vTYAso)[[3]](/library/6kdjKJ0)[[10]](/library/bOdHIJ0)

* If <u>folate</u> level is normal, obtain either: 

* Plasma <u>homocysteine</u>: ↑ (sensitive, but not specific)

* <u>RBC</u> <u>folate</u>: ↓





### Additional evaluation




Consider further assessment based on the suspected underlying cause.




* Assessment of <u>nutritional status</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for malabsorption</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for celiac disease</u>

* <u>Diagnostics for alcohol use disorder</u>

---

## Treatment

* Initiate <u>folate</u> replacement in patients with confirmed <u>folate</u> deficiency. [[2]](/library/vTYAso)[[3]](/library/6kdjKJ0)

* <u>Folic acid</u> DOSAGE

* Duration of treatment depends on the underlying cause.

* Encourage consumption of <u>folate-rich foods</u>, e.g., leafy green vegetables, fruits, and fortified foods.

* Manage the underlying condition.

* See also “<u>Folic acid supplementation in pregnancy</u>.”





> [!WARNING]
> In combined <u>vitamin B<sub>12</sub></u> and <u>folate</u> deficiency, <u>folate</u> replacement without <u>vitamin B<sub>12</sub></u> may exacerbate neurological symptoms. Rule out <u>vitamin B<sub>12</sub> deficiency</u> before starting <u>folate</u> replacement. [[11]](/library/CidqFp0)




> [!NOTE]
> <u>Folic acid supplementation</u> is recommended for all individuals planning or capable of <u>pregnancy</u> because of the risk of <u>neural tube defects</u> due to maternal <u>folate</u> deficiency. [[12]](/library/46Y3OJ)

---

## Prevention

* <u>Prevention of folate deficiency</u> includes:

* Adequate dietary intake of <u>folate-rich foods</u> in all individuals

* <u>Folic acid supplementation</u> in all individuals capable of <u>pregnancy</u> (see “<u>Folic acid supplementation in pregnancy</u>”) [[14]](/library/okd0KJ0)

* Folate-rich foods include:

* Leafy green vegetables

* Fortified foods (e.g., breads, pastas, cereals)

* Legumes

* Fruits (e.g., citrus fruits) [[3]](/library/6kdjKJ0)

* Other: nuts, eggs, meat [[3]](/library/6kdjKJ0)





| <br>Recommended dietary intake of <u>folate</u> [[13]](/library/pAdLks0) |  |
| --- | --- |
| Age | Intake |
| 0–6 months | 65 mcg |
| 7–12 months | 80 mcg |
| 1–3 years | 150 mcg |
| 4–8 years | 200 mcg |
| 9–13 years | 300 mcg |
| ≥ 14 years | 400 mcg |
